evidence_items.locator: Section 'OpenAI', paragraph beginning 'We’re hoping to grow OpenAI'

receipt.public_excerpt: We’ll freely collaborate with others across many institutions and expect to work with companies to research and deploy new technologies.

evidence_items.explanation: The surrounding paragraph encourages publication and promises collaboration and patent sharing. It does not expressly promise release of all future source code, making the scope of the allegedly broken pledge consequential.

evidence_items.locator: Paragraph beginning 'In one telling exchange from January 2016'

receipt.public_excerpt: As we get closer to building AI, it will make sense to start being less open.

evidence_items.explanation: The reproduced email explicitly links near-term sharing to recruitment and anticipates later restrictions. It supports those components, but its endorsement of actual near-term sharing does not establish a wholly insincere pledge.

evidence_items.locator: May 2016 meeting with Dario Amodei, immediately after Altman's statement about source-code release

receipt.public_excerpt: But let’s please not try to correct that.

evidence_items.explanation: The reported exchange supports deliberate reluctance to correct an overly broad public understanding of openness. It does not independently establish leaders' intentions when making the December 2015 pledge.

unresolved_gaps: No located record establishes that the actual 2015 commitments were knowingly insincere when made.
Recruitment was an explicit consideration, but the records do not establish that it was the only motive.
The difference between encouraging publication and promising unrestricted future release prevents a decisive inference about non-performance.
